title: Stale drain-state tombstones caused inflight cross-region misrouting — incident retro and fixes
creator: Asha Nair
description: Summary: On 2025-01-11 a regional drain transition produced stale 'drain tombstone' state in the routing cache, allowing inflight traffic and new requests to be routed to a region that had been marked draining. That region's autoscaler was concurrently scaling down GPU pools; several requests hit fallback paths that selected incompatible model variants (cross-architecture quantized variant on a CPU host), producing runtime errors and cascading fallbacks. Impacted customers experienced elevated 5xx rates and latency spikes for ~35 minutes. This ticket documents the incident timeline, root causes, remediation, and permanent mitigations.
timeline:
2025-01-11 09:12 UTC: On-call alert - increased 5xx and latency from API layer.
2025-01-11 09:14 UTC: Initial paging and quick triage, identified routing weight oscillation toward eu-west-2.
2025-01-11 09:18 UTC: Noticed a draining operation initiated ~09:10 but region weight did not reach 0; routing cache reported a 'tombstone' drain marker with stale expiry.
2025-01-11 09:22 UTC: Traffic continued to be routed; autoscaler preemptively reclaimed some GPU instances in the region.
2025-01-11 09:26 UTC: Several requests hit fallback model variants; runtime logs showed variant loader errors (unsupported quantized format on CPU host).
2025-01-11 09:30 UTC: Engineering applied emergency global clamp: forcibly set region routing weight to 0 and disabled fallbacks to incompatible variants.
2025-01-11 09:40 UTC: Error rate trended down; full recovery by 09:48 UTC.
2025-01-11 09:55 UTC: Post-incident triage meeting held; owners assigned for immediate and long-term fixes.
impact: Peak 5xx rate to public API: 3.7% (baseline ~0.02%). Median p95 latency increased 4x for affected routes. Error budget consumed ~12% for eu-west-2 customers over incident window. ~7 paying customers reported degraded responses; two customers had production failures requiring rollback of features.
root_cause: Three contributing failures: 1) routing cache logic allowed a 'drain tombstone' to persist past its intended TTL when concurrent drain signals and a partial config update occurred, leaving a stale state that did not zero region weight in decision stage; 2) routing decision path evaluated configured fallbacks after weight calculation rather than pre-checking variant compatibility, allowing cross-architecture fallback selection; 3) autoscaler reclaimed resources based on drain signal without coordination with the routing controller, creating a small window where requests routed to a region with insufficient compatible hardware.
actions_taken:
Immediate: 1) Emergency rule applied to clamp eu-west-2 weight to 0 and block fallback selection to incompatible variants at 09:30 UTC. 2) Rehydrated routing cache from authoritative control-plane snapshot to remove tombstone entries. 3) Rolled back a nonblocking config replication change that was mid-flight.
Short-term: 1) Deployed hotfix (PR #4678) to add expedited tombstone expiry and atomic region weight update. 2) Added compatibility checks in routing path to veto fallback variants that don't match host architecture. 3) Temporarily increased canary frequency in eu regions to surface similar regressions earlier.
permanent_fixes: 1) Routing decision pipeline change: drain flag evaluation moved to the earliest stage and region weights are updated transactionally with control-plane versioning (deploy in runtime-1.22). 2) Introduce a 'variant compatibility matrix' in the model catalog that the routing planner consults before fallback selection. 3) Autoscaler-routing handshake: autoscaler will publish planned reclamation windows; routing controller will treat planned reclamation as 'soft drain' and avoid routing new requests until reclamation completes. 4) Add unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent drain + config update + autoscaler events.
monitoring_and_alerting: New alerts created: 'routing.drain_state_mismatch' (Fired when drain flag != authoritative control-plane state for >30s), 'variant.fallback_compatibility_error' (Fired on >5 errors/min), 'region.weight_oscillation' (Fired when weight changes >50% within 60s). Dashboards: added 'Drain transitions and weight consistency' panel to Console; linked Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/route-drain. Postmortem dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/incident-10023-snapshot.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-10040 - implement transactional region-weight API (owner: Lina Gomez)
ENG-10057 - catalog compatibility matrix and routing checks (owner: Wei Zhang)
ENG-10110 - autoscaler-routing handshake protocol + integration tests (owner: Marcus Lee)
ENG-10122 - add synthetic canaries for drain-state correctness (owner: Priya Patel)
test_and_validation: Hotfix was validated via canary rollout: 5% of traffic to eu regions for 30 minutes with synthetic traffic; no recurrence over 48 hours. Unit and integration test coverage increased: added 6 new tests simulating concurrent drain/config-update and 3 tests for fallback veto logic. Post-deploy chaos run performed: simulated autoscaler reclaim + concurrent drain; routing honored weight = 0 and fallbacks were vetoed.
communication_and_links: Incident bridge logs: https://zoom.redwood/incident-10023-bridge. Postmortem doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.company/display/INF/ENG-10023+drain-tombstone+retro. Emergency PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4678. Follow-up roadmap entry: https://product.redwood.company/roadmap/smart-routing.
lessons_learned: 1) Control-plane state is the single source of truth; caches must have strict expiry and reconciliation. 2) Routing decisions must validate assumptions (host architecture, resource availability) before selecting fallback variants. 3) System interactions (autoscaler <-> routing) require explicit coordination to avoid safe-state windows where a region reports drained but still receives traffic.
notes: On-call rotation handled escalation well; timeline for mitigation from first page to clamp rule was ~18 minutes. We recommend a postmortem review session with SRE, autoscaler, and routing owners in Cycle 49 to validate the handshake protocol design.
